title: Wren and the Spire
premise: Lior Vasquez, the royal food-taster who secretly sells outlawed charms, survives the night the stars go out only because a street-thief named Wren pulls him from a burning market. Wren, it turns out, carries a fragment of the Spire—the anchor-stone of the covenant that once bound the human and fae realms, and whose fall caused both the darkness and the collapse of the border wards. Hunted by the usurper's inquisitors, the two flee toward the free cities, gathering the scattered covenant-bearers while Lior's slow-built poison immunity becomes the key to surviving the Spire's trials. At the climax, Lior offers his own memories—twenty years of careful anonymity—as mortar to reforge the covenant, and the restored stars burn away the usurper's claim. In the end, Lior remembers almost nothing of his old life, but Wren remembers for both of them, and the city that outlawed magic learns to belong to both worlds at once.
about_author: E. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town where the fog rolls in early and the streetlights flicker, allegedly on schedule.

chapters.title: The Taster's Table
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. We meet him at the palace, swallowing a suspect dish with practiced calm, then slipping into the night market to sell a memory-charm to a desperate widow. Establishes his double life and the law against magic. Emotional beat: the quiet loneliness of a man who has made himself essential and invisible at once.

chapters.title: Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The stars vanish, the border wards shatter, and the market district burns as panic spreads. Wren, a quick-fingered thief, finds Lior half-dead in the smoke and drags him into the undercity. Emotional beat: terror giving way to a stubborn, unexpected instinct to save a stranger.

chapters.title: What the Thief Carried
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Wren reveals the shard of Spire-stone she stole years ago, the thing the inquisitors are tearing the city apart to find. Lior recognizes its resonance from his taster's training—his body has been quietly absorbing ward-poisons for twenty years, making him uniquely able to touch it. Emotional beat: the shock of discovering his invisibility was preparation.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Edict
chapters.summary: Dual POV, alternating. Inquisitor-General Corvane declares martial law and posts Wren's likeness on every gate, while the free cities' council debates surrender. Lior and Wren slip past the checkpoints with help from the widow Lior once charmed. Emotional beat: the cost of small kindnesses, repaid at scale.

chapters.title: Road of Hollow Bells
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The road to the first free city, through villages where the wards' fall has let old fae debts resurface. Wren's shard hums near a standing stone, and a fae herald names her 'bearer'—a title she never asked for. Emotional beat: resentment at being chosen, and the first stirrings of trust between her and Lior.

chapters.title: The Covenant-Bearers
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In the free city of Marrowgate they find two other bearers: a disgraced scholar and a child who dreams the Spire's geometry. Lior's immunity lets him read the shard without burning, and he learns the covenant demands a willing sacrifice of memory from each bearer. Emotional beat: dread braided with belonging—he has found a family precisely when it may cost him everything.

chapters.title: Corvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV, the book's only villain chapter. We learn he was once a bearer who refused the sacrifice and seized the Spire's power instead, and that the usurper's armies march under his false starlight. He offers Lior amnesty and his old life back in exchange for the shard. Emotional beat: the seductive logic of a man who chose safety over covenant—and the reader's fear Lior might agree.

chapters.title: The Siege of Marrowgate
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The usurper's army arrives; the child bearer is captured, and the scholar falls holding the gate. Wren wants to run with the shard; Lior chooses to trade himself for the child. Emotional beat: grief and fury, and Wren's realization that she loves the stubborn taster enough to follow him into the dark.

chapters.title: The Spire Remembers
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, captive in the usurper's citadel built atop the Spire's root. He endures Corvane's interrogations—his poison-trained body shrugging off truth-serums—while Wren and the child infiltrate. In the Spire's heart, Lior understands the covenant: it does not take memory by force; it asks. Emotional beat: stillness before the storm, and a choice made freely.

chapters.title: Stars, Reforged
chapters.summary: Dual POV for the climax and resolution. The bearers gather at the Spire; Corvane makes his last bid for its power and is unmade by the covenant he abandoned. Lior gives up his twenty years of careful anonymity, and the stars return as the usurper's armies falter. Epilogue beat: a taster with no past tends a small stall beside a thief who tells him, every morning, who he was—and who he is becoming.
